title: Drainage Response-Law Family and Sensitivity Characterization Evidence
material_findings: DRAMET=1 is piecewise linear in abs(gwl), with derivative discontinuities at unequal-slope knots and potentially at gwl=0.
DRAMET=2 admits analytic stable-branch sensitivities for IPOS 1..5, but IPOS=4 has an interface kink when kvtop differs from kvbot.
The legacy diffl=1e-10 cutoff is representation-sensitive when reconstructed from gwl, zbotdr and shape; no modern normalized cutoff policy is qualified here.
Legacy DRAMET=2 input ranges admit zero values for parameters used in division/logarithms; a production candidate requires stricter mathematical-domain validation.
For empirical interflow with admitted exponent below one, dq/dgwl diverges as activation is approached from above; no uniformly bounded implicit tangent exists on that legacy domain.
For multi-level drainage, stable-branch total sensitivity is the sum of per-level sensitivities, while nonsmoothness is the union of level branch points.
